semantic_closure.statement:
For every fixed finite \(K\), the routine \(\mathfrak C_K\) gives an arbitrary-\(\varepsilon\) validated certificate in the following extended-value sense.  Fix a declared face \(A\subseteq\mathcal K\) with \(|A|\geq2\) and a compact rational cell of positive \((v_A,r_A)\) on which \(\Omega_A\) is uniformly positive definite.  A deterministic algorithm enumerates every nonempty retained subset \(S\subseteq A\), invokes the compact certificates at explicitly computed radii \(M_S\), and returns a represented randomized selector and outward-rounded numbers satisfying
\[
L^{\infty}_{\varepsilon,A}\leq G_A(v_A,r_A)
\leq \sup_{h\in\mathbb R^A}\mathbb E_h\!\left[\max_{k\in A}h_k-h_{\delta(X)}\right]
\leq U^{\infty}_{\varepsilon,A},
\qquad U^{\infty}_{\varepsilon,A}-L^{\infty}_{\varepsilon,A}\leq\varepsilon.
\]
For every retained non-singleton \(S\), the primitive oracle transfer uses a compact representative set \(\mathscr H_{S,M_S}\subseteq\mathbb R^S\) whose quotient classes cover the full closed quotient radius-\(M_S\) ball; the singleton quotient is trivial and uses its exact zero-risk rule.  The routine makes the independent Gaussian split explicit: the screening observation has covariance \(\Sigma(v_A,r_A)/\lambda\), the decision observation has covariance \(\Sigma(v_A,r_A)/(1-\lambda)\), and the compact selector receives the decision observation multiplied by \(\sqrt{1-\lambda}\).  Coordinates within a fixed threshold of the screening maximum are retained.  Hence partial-tie limits such as \((0,-a,-M)\) enter their retained lower-dimensional game rather than an invalid radial truncation.  Uniformity is over retained subsets of this declared face; global adaptation over every candidate policy requires taking \(A=\mathcal K\) with positive information for every candidate.

The same routine certifies both outer designs.  Over \(p\in\Delta_K\), it returns a risk interval of width at most \(\varepsilon\), rational simplex cells containing every minimizer of \(p\mapsto G_A(v_A,(Bp)_A)\), and a feasible \(\varepsilon\)-optimal \(p\).  Over \(a\in\Delta_A\), it returns the analogous objects for \(a\mapsto G_A(v_A,a)\).  A zero action-relevant coordinate has the proved extended value \(+\infty\); a computable two-arm lower bound excludes a whole boundary neighborhood before finite interior branch-and-bound.

For primitive implementation, partition the \(C\) clusters into three disjoint prespecified pieces of sizes \(m_C\), \(N_C^{\mathrm s}\), and \(N_C^{\mathrm d}\), where \(m_C\to\infty\), \(m_C/C\to0\), \(N_C^{\mathrm s}/C\to\lambda\), and \(N_C^{\mathrm d}/C\to1-\lambda\).  Form separate calibrated screening and decision estimators.  Their \(\sqrt C\)-limits have covariances \(\Sigma/\lambda\) and \(\Sigma/(1-\lambda)\), respectively, and the compact selector is applied to \(\sqrt{1-\lambda}\) times the decision statistic.  With pilot covariance snapping, the asymptotic scaled simple regret is uniformly bounded by the certified Gaussian upper value over the Bernoulli outer simplex and over each compact active-interior exact-count allocation set.  For every retained non-singleton face \(S\), the face-indexed covering condition identifies the primitive supremum with the full-ball quantity \(G_{S,M_S}\) before the face risks are assembled; the singleton branch remains exact.  The transfer is simultaneous over the finitely many retained subsets of the declared face and over triangular bounded-schedule arrays whose covariance stays in the certified cells.  Fixed-scale inferior policies have vanishing scaled contribution; \(C^{-1/2}\)-scale policies enter the retained compact game.  For global candidate adaptation take \(A=\mathcal K\); under exact counts this also requires all candidate shares in a compact simplex interior.  At a vanishing action-relevant share only \(+\infty\) is asserted.  A diagonal sequence of tolerances, split fractions, pilot sizes, and certificate meshes transfers the certified noncompact Gaussian value and outer design on exactly these domains.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
We prove the three assertions: certification of the unbounded Gaussian game, certification of the two outer design problems, and uniform transfer to the primitive experiments.

\emph{1. Certification of the unbounded Gaussian game.}
Fix the declared face \(A\), put \(d=|A|\), and first work on one compact rational cell from the statement.  Write
\[
\Sigma=\Sigma(v_A,r_A)=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_i^2:i\in A),
\qquad \sigma_i^2=v_i/r_i.
\]
Positivity and compactness of this cell give computable constants \(0<\underline\sigma\leq\overline\sigma<\infty\) such that every \(\sigma_i\) lies in \([\underline\sigma,\overline\sigma]\).  Hence all quotient covariance matrices in the cell are uniformly positive definite, as required by \(\texttt{thm:gaussian-finite-certificate}\).

We first obtain a finite cellwise upper bound.  Let \(b\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{i\in A}h_i\), put \(d_i=h_b-h_i\geq0\), and use \(\delta_0(X)\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{i\in A}X_i\), with deterministic tie breaking.  If \(\delta_0(X)=i\ne b\), then \(X_i-X_b\geq0\).  Since \(X_i-X_b\sim N(-d_i,\sigma_i^2+\sigma_b^2)\), the union bound gives
\[
\mathbb E_h\{h_b-h_{\delta_0(X)}\}
\leq\sum_{i\ne b}d_i\Phi\!\left(-\frac{d_i}{\sqrt{\sigma_i^2+\sigma_b^2}}\right).       \tag{1}
\]
For \(x\geq0\), integration by parts gives \(x\Phi(-x)\leq\varphi(x)\leq(2\pi)^{-1/2}\), and \(\sqrt{\sigma_i^2+\sigma_b^2}\leq\sqrt2\,\overline\sigma\).  Therefore
\[
G_A(v_A,r_A)\leq H_0:=\frac{(d-1)\overline\sigma}{\sqrt\pi}.       \tag{2}
\]

Choose rational \(0<\lambda<1\), then rational \(T>0\), so that, with \(a_\lambda=\sqrt{2/\lambda}\,\overline\sigma\),
\[
\{(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}-1\}H_0<\frac\varepsilon4,
\qquad
\frac{2d^2a_\lambda}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
e^{-T^2/(2a_\lambda^2)}<\frac\varepsilon4.                        \tag{3}
\]
Such rational choices exist because the first expression tends to zero as \(\lambda\downarrow0\), and, for fixed \(\lambda\), the second tends to zero as \(T\to\infty\).  Directed rational interval evaluation verifies the strict inequalities in finite time.

For every nonempty \(S\subseteq A\), choose a rational radius
\[
M_S\geq2\sqrt{1-\lambda}\,T\sqrt{|S|-1}.                          \tag{4}
\]
For a singleton use exact risk zero.  For \(|S|\geq2\), apply \(\texttt{thm:gaussian-finite-certificate}\) on the induced compact positive covariance cell, with a common rational accuracy \(\eta>0\) satisfying
\[
(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}\eta<\frac\varepsilon4.                         \tag{5}
\]
It returns \(L_S\leq G_{S,M_S}(v_S,r_S)\leq U_S\), with \(U_S-L_S\leq\eta\), and a represented selector.  Define
\[
L_A^0=\max_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq A}L_S,
\qquad
U_A^0=(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}\max_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq A}U_S
+\frac{2d^2a_\lambda}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-T^2/(2a_\lambda^2)}.       \tag{6}
\]
The lower inequality in \(\texttt{lem:hierarchical-gaussian-screening}\) yields
\[
L_A^0\leq\max_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq A}G_{S,M_S}(v_S,r_S)
\leq G_A(v_A,r_A).                                                 \tag{7}
\]
The selector constructed in that lemma uses the independent screen with covariance \(\Sigma/\lambda\), retains coordinates within \(T\) of its maximum, and applies the appropriate compact selector to \(\sqrt{1-\lambda}\) times the independent decision observation.  Its risk is at most \(U_A^0\), so
\[
G_A(v_A,r_A)\leq
\sup_{h\in\mathbb R^A}\mathbb E_h\!\left[\max_{i\in A}h_i-h_{\delta(X)}\right]
\leq U_A^0.                                                        \tag{8}
\]
If \(S_\star\) maximizes \(U_S\), then
\[
\max_SU_S=U_{S_\star}\leq L_{S_\star}+\eta\leq L_A^0+\eta.      \tag{9}
\]
Also (2) and (7) give \(L_A^0\leq H_0\).  Equations (3), (5), (6), and (9) imply
\[
U_A^0-L_A^0
\leq\{(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}-1\}H_0+(1-\lambda)^{-1/2}\eta
+\frac{2d^2a_\lambda}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-T^2/(2a_\lambda^2)}
<\frac{3\varepsilon}{4}.                                         \tag{10}
\]
Choose the working precision so that outward rounding enlarges the gap by less than \(\varepsilon/4\).  The rounded values \(L^\infty_{\varepsilon,A}\) and \(U^\infty_{\varepsilon,A}\) then satisfy the first displayed chain and have gap at most \(\varepsilon\).  There are \(2^d-1\) nonempty subsets, so all compact calls and finite rational searches terminate.  Concatenating their receipts with the rational witnesses for (3)--(5), the subset list, the tail enclosure, and the rounding record gives a machine-checkable transcript.  Because the routine ranges over all retained subsets, a configuration with only a proper subset of locally tied coordinates enters that subset's game; no radial restriction on the full vector has been imposed.

\emph{2. Certification of the outer designs.}
Under \(\mathsf B(p)\), \(\texttt{def:hit-map}\) and \(\texttt{lem:exact-hit-factorization}\) give \(q=Bp\).  Every entry of \(B\) is positive, so
\[
(Bp)_k\geq\underline q_k:=\min_{\ell\in\mathcal K}B_{k\ell}>0
\quad(p\in\Delta_K,\ k\in A).                                   \tag{11}
\]
Partition the rational simplex into rational cells.  Linear interval arithmetic gives coordinatewise bounds \(q^-\leq Bp\leq q^+\) on each cell.  By \(\texttt{lem:gaussian-information-order}\), a certified lower bound for \(G_A(v_A,q^+)\) is valid throughout the cell, whereas any feasible rational point gives an upper incumbent.  If \((1-\xi)q\leq q'\leq(1+\xi)q\), with \(0<\xi<1\), the same lemma gives
\[
(1+\xi)^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,q)
\leq G_A(v_A,q')
\leq(1-\xi)^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,q).                                    \tag{12}
\]
The factors tend uniformly to one as \(\xi\downarrow0\), (11) makes all relative cell widths uniformly refinable, and (2) makes the values uniformly finite.  Rational branch-and-bound, with a summable numerical error allocation among calls to Part 1, therefore terminates with an interval of prescribed width, keeps every cell containing a minimizer, and returns a feasible \(\varepsilon\)-optimal rational point.

For exact counts, the feasible rates satisfy
\[
a_i\geq0\quad(i\in A),\qquad\sum_{i\in A}a_i=1.                 \tag{13}
\]
An action-relevant zero coordinate has value \(+\infty\) by \(\texttt{lem:gaussian-information-order}\).  For distinct \(i,j\in A\), the subface inequality in \(\texttt{lem:hierarchical-gaussian-screening}\) and \(\texttt{thm:two-policy-minimax}\) give
\[
G_A(v_A,a)\geq G_{\{i,j\}}(v_{\{i,j\}},a_{\{i,j\}})
=\kappa\sqrt{\frac{v_i}{a_i}+\frac{v_j}{a_j}}
\geq\kappa\sqrt{\frac{v_i}{a_i}}.                               \tag{14}
\]
Let \(\underline v>0\) be a rational lower enclosure for all \(v_i\), and let \(\overline U<\infty\) be a certified upper bound at the uniform allocation.  Choose rational
\[
0<\eta_0<\min\left\{\frac1{2d},
\frac{\kappa^2\underline v}{4(\overline U+1)^2}\right\}.         \tag{15}
\]
If \(a_i<\eta_0\), then (14)--(15) give \(G_A(v_A,a)>2(\overline U+1)>\overline U\).  Thus no minimizer lies there.  The minimizers lie in the compact rational polytope (13) with \(a_i\geq\eta_0\), where the argument based on (12) applies.  This proves the exact-count outer certificate without evaluating a positive-rate formula on the boundary.

\emph{3. Uniform transfer to the primitive experiments.}
Partition the clusters into pilot, screening, and decision pieces with
\[
m_C+N_C^{\mathrm s}+N_C^{\mathrm d}=C,
\quad m_C\to\infty,
\quad m_C/C\to0,
\quad N_C^{\mathrm s}/C\to\lambda,
\quad N_C^{\mathrm d}/C\to1-\lambda.                              \tag{16}
\]
For exact-count randomization, make the analogous split within every active fixed-count stratum.  Assumptions \(\texttt{ass:iid-schedules}\), \(\texttt{ass:bernoulli-label-schedule-independence}\), and \(\texttt{ass:cr-label-schedule-independence}\) give independence of the outcome arrays in the three pieces, conditionally on their prescribed design counts.  The assignment laws are those in \(\texttt{ass:bernoulli-label-iid}\), \(\texttt{ass:bernoulli-units}\), \(\texttt{ass:cr-label-vector}\), and \(\texttt{ass:cr-exact-slices}\); \(\texttt{ass:isolated-clusters}\) makes the observed reward the corresponding within-cluster potential outcome.

For \(z\in\mathcal S_k\), \(\texttt{lem:exact-hit-factorization}\) gives
\[
\rho_z=\Pr(Z_c=z)=\frac{q_k}{M_k}
\geq\frac{\min_\ell B_{k\ell}}{M_k}>0.                           \tag{17}
\]
In the certified exact-count region, the corresponding limiting cell frequency is at least \(\eta_0/M_k\).  There are finitely many target cells.  On the event that every empirical cell frequency is at least half its lower bound, the ratio identity applied cellwise gives, for \(b\in\{\mathrm s,\mathrm d\}\),
\[
\widetilde U_{C,k}^{\,b}-U_k
=\frac1{N_C^b}\sum_{c\in b}
\frac{\mathbf1\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}}{q_k}
\{W_c(Z_c)-\mu_{Z_c}\}+o_P((N_C^b)^{-1/2}),                     \tag{18}
\]
uniformly in the Bernoulli design; under exact counts, \(q_k\) is replaced by the active stratum share.  Indeed, write each cell mean as its empirical centered sum divided by its empirical frequency and replace the reciprocal frequency by its probability reciprocal.  The centered numerator and frequency error are each \(O_P((N_C^b)^{-1/2})\), so their product is \(O_P((N_C^b)^{-1})\); a finite cell sum preserves the remainder.  The empty-cell fallback occurs with exponentially small probability by (17).

The summands in (18) are centered and uniformly bounded.  Their coordinate variances are \(\tau_k^2/q_k\) under Bernoulli assignment and \(\tau_k^2/a_k\) under exact counts, and distinct coordinates have zero product because the slices are disjoint.  For every fixed linear combination, third-order Taylor expansion of its characteristic function and summation of the \(O((N_C^b)^{-3/2})\) remainders give the corresponding centered normal characteristic function.  Since this holds for every linear combination, the vector limits are jointly
\[
\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_C^{\mathrm s}-U\}
\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma/\lambda),
\qquad
\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_C^{\mathrm d}-U\}
\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma/(1-\lambda)),                             \tag{19}
\]
with independent limits.  Under a \(C^{-1/2}\)-local displacement \(h\), both limiting means are \(h\).  Hence the screening statistic has covariance \(\Sigma/\lambda\), while
\[
\sqrt{1-\lambda}\,\sqrt C
\{\widetilde U_C^{\mathrm d}-U(P_0)\}                             \tag{20}
\]
has covariance \(\Sigma\) and mean \(\sqrt{1-\lambda}h\).  Since the tied active baseline is a multiple of \(\mathbf1_A\), location invariance removes it; undoing the scale multiplies regret by \((1-\lambda)^{-1/2}\), exactly as in (6).

We now verify the facewise coverage needed to invoke the primitive transfer.  For every retained \(S\subseteq A\) with \(|S|\geq2\), the matrix \(D_S\) has full row rank.  Set
\[
J_S=D_S^{\prime}(D_SD_S^{\prime})^{-1},
\qquad
\mathscr H_{S,M_S}=\{J_Sg:g\in\mathbb R^{|S|-1},\ \lVert g\rVert_2\leq M_S\}.             \tag{21}
\]
The closed Euclidean ball is compact and \(J_S\) is continuous, so \(\mathscr H_{S,M_S}\) is compact.  Moreover \(D_SJ_S=I\), whence
\[
D_S\mathscr H_{S,M_S}=\{g:\lVert g\rVert_2\leq M_S\},
\quad\text{equivalently}\quad
\{[u]:u\in\mathscr H_{S,M_S}\}
=\{[w]\in H_S:\lVert[w]\rVert_S\leq M_S\}.                     \tag{22}
\]
For a singleton set take \(\mathscr H_{S,0}=\{0\}\); its quotient and regret are zero.  On the good screening event, \(\texttt{lem:hierarchical-gaussian-screening}\) gives
\[
\lVert[\sqrt{1-\lambda}h_S]\rVert_S
\leq2\sqrt{1-\lambda}\,T\sqrt{|S|-1}\leq M_S.                  \tag{23}
\]
By (22), some \(h_S^\star\in\mathscr H_{S,M_S}\) has the same quotient coordinate as \(\sqrt{1-\lambda}h_S\).  Their difference lies in \(\ker D_S=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1_S\}\).  The Gaussian selector and regret are translation invariant by \(\texttt{lem:gaussian-quotient-reduction}\), so their risks agree.  The repaired \(\texttt{prop:oracle-transfer-bernoulli}\) or \(\texttt{prop:oracle-transfer-cr}\), applied on \(\mathscr H_{S,M_S}\), therefore controls every point of the full compact quotient ball in (23), not merely a chosen compact subset.  Thus it transfers exactly \(G_{S,M_S}\).  This facewise equality is invoked before taking the maximum over retained subsets in (6), and the finite maximum preserves uniform convergence.

For pilot covariance consistency, let \(\rho_0>0\) be the minimum of the finitely many lower bounds in (17) and \(\eta_0/M_k\).  For a piece of size \(N\), exponential Markov applied to a cell count gives constants \(c>0\) such that
\[
\Pr\{N_z^{(N)}\leq N\rho_z/2\}\leq e^{-cN}                       \tag{24}
\]
uniformly over \(\rho_z\geq\rho_0\).  Conditional variances of bounded cell means and second moments are \(O(1/N_z^{(N)})\).  Hence Chebyshev's inequality, (24), and a finite union bound prove uniform covariance consistency and valid outward snapping.  Applying the same bounded-sum argument to the screening piece gives uniform constants \(c_1,c_2>0\) with
\[
\Pr\!\left\{\sqrt C\,|\widetilde U_{C,k}^{\mathrm s}-U_k|>x\right\}
\leq c_1e^{-c_2x^2}+c_1e^{-c_2C},
\qquad 0\leq x\leq\sqrt C.                                      \tag{25}
\]
The pairwise decomposition in \(\texttt{lem:hierarchical-gaussian-screening}\) and (25) give a deterministic remainder tending to zero as \(T\to\infty\) for deleting a best coordinate or retaining a set whose scaled range exceeds \(2T\).  Thus a policy with diverging scaled welfare gap contributes \(o(1)\) to scaled regret.

It remains to justify uniformity over bounded-schedule triangular arrays.  If it failed, the compact schedule space \([0,1]^{n\times\mathcal Z_n}\) and \(\texttt{lem:weak-compactness-compact-laws}\) would give a weakly convergent subsequence of a violating sequence of laws.  Assignment-specific welfare means and variances converge because the relevant coordinates and their squares are bounded continuous functions.  Passing to a further subsequence makes every nonnegative scaled policy gap converge in \([0,\infty]\).  Infinite limiting gaps have vanishing contribution by (25).  On the remaining coordinates, the bounded triangular-array characteristic-function calculation proving (19), pilot consistency, and covariance snapping give joint convergence of pilot, screen, and decision statistics.  The finitely represented selectors have Gaussian-null affine boundaries.  Bounded truncation followed by (25) transfers expected scaled regret to the Gaussian screened selector.  Equations (21)--(23) then place each retained non-singleton face in its full compact quotient game, while the singleton branch is exact; the Gaussian risk bound (8) contradicts the assumed violation.  This proves the asserted uniformity over all retained faces and certified covariance cells.

For \(A=\mathcal K\), (11) supplies positive information for every Bernoulli candidate.  For exact counts, Part 2 puts every optimizer in a compact simplex interior, the domain of the primitive exact-count transfer.  At a vanishing action-relevant share, \(\texttt{lem:gaussian-information-order}\) supplies only the extended value \(+\infty\).  Fixed-scale inferior policies have diverging scaled gaps and vanish by (25), whereas \(C^{-1/2}\)-scale policies remain in a retained compact game.

Finally, at stage \(j\), run Parts 1 and 2 with tolerance \(1/j\), choose the rational split, threshold, full-ball representative sets (21), compact radii, and meshes, and then choose \(C_j\) so that all pilot, split-limit, snapping, screening, and facewise-transfer errors are at most \(1/j\), with all subsample sizes diverging and \(m_C/C\leq1/j\).  Keeping the stage-\(j\) choices for \(C_j\leq C<C_{j+1}\) gives a diagonal sequence.  Equations (6)--(25) transfer the certified noncompact Gaussian risk and both outer designs to the primitive calibrated experiments on exactly the domains in the statement.
semantic_closure.justification: The screened construction reduces every unbounded configuration to one of finitely many full-ball certified quotient games, and the repaired primitive transfers cover every one of those balls.
semantic_closure.gap: The former radial construction and arbitrary compact representative sets missed lower-dimensional near ties and could omit quotient directions; subset screening plus facewise surjective representative sets close both gaps.
semantic_closure.consumer: A prospective saturation experiment can certify either outer allocation and deploy the calibrated selector with uniform protection over partial ties on the stated positive-rate domains.

semantic_closure.gap: Existing two-stage variance formulas target direct and spillover contrasts rather than the full calibrated exact-slice welfare vector.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every fixed \(C\), fixed label-count vector, and bounded target-only loss \(\mathcal L\), regime \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\) satisfies
\[
\inf_{\delta\in\mathfrak D_C}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[\mathcal L(U,\delta(\mathcal E_{C,CR}^{\mathrm{full}}(\alpha)))]
=
\inf_{\delta\in\mathfrak D_C}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[\mathcal L(U,\delta(\mathcal E_{C,CR}^{\mathrm{hit}}(\alpha)))].
\]
More generally, the equality holds after replacing the displayed finite deployment action space and its rule class by any standard-Borel decision space and all measurable randomized rules, provided the loss is bounded and target-only; this includes the ranking action of Han--Owusu--Shin.  Here the reduced experiment deletes the randomized label vector after the realized exact-count assignments are recorded.
semantic_closure.justification: The exact-count benchmark must be stated as its own randomization experiment.
semantic_closure.gap: Two-stage design papers retain strategy labels, while the exact count itself identifies the target slice in this menu.
semantic_closure.consumer: This gives the clean exact-count experiment used as the mechanism benchmark.

semantic_closure.statement: Under \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), with \(\alpha_k>0\) and nondegenerate slice variance for every reported \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(\widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}\to_P\Sigma_{CR}^{(K)}\), and \[\liminf_{C\to\infty}\inf_{P:\min_{k\in\mathcal K}\tau_k^2(P)\geq\underline\tau^2}\Pr_P\{\operatorname{Rank}_k(U)\subseteq\mathcal R_{C,k}(\gamma)\text{ for every }k\in\mathcal K\}\geq1-\gamma,\] uniformly over partial ties.
semantic_closure.justification: The complete-randomization rank theorem is separate from the Bernoulli hit-count theorem.
semantic_closure.gap: Generic two-stage Wald theory does not state set-valued exact-slice rank coverage at partial ties.
semantic_closure.consumer: Exact-count studies can report rank ranges under their actual fixed allocation.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Write \(C_k=C_{C,k}\) and \(a_{C,k}=C_k/C\).  The all-share assumption gives \(a_{C,k}\to\alpha_k>0\), uniformly bounded away from zero for large \(C\).  Conditional on the fixed label vector, the observations are independent and uniform on their assigned slices.  For \(z\in\mathcal S_k\), set
\[
S_z=\sum_{c:L_c=k}\mathbf1\{Z_c=z\}\{W_c(z)-\mu_z\}.
\]
On occupied cells,
\[
\sqrt C(\widetilde U_{C,k}-U_k)
=C^{-1/2}\sum_{c=1}^C\frac{C}{C_k}\mathbf1\{L_c=k\}
\{W_c(Z_c)-\mu_{Z_c}\}+R_{C,k}. \tag{75}
\]
Conditional variance calculations give \(N_z-C_k/M_k=O_P(\sqrt{C_k})\) and \(S_z=O_P(\sqrt{C_k})\), uniformly over bounded schedule laws.  Since the number of cells is fixed and \(C_k\asymp C\), the cell-ratio remainder satisfies \(\max_k|R_{C,k}|=o_P(1)\) uniformly.  Also
\[
\Pr\{\text{some target cell empty}\}
\leq\sum_kM_ke^{-C_k/M_k}\to0. \tag{76}
\]
The conditional covariance of the leading term in (75) is diagonal with entries
\[
\frac{C}{C_k}\frac1{M_k}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\operatorname{Var}_P\{W(z)\}
=\frac{\tau_k^2(P)}{a_{C,k}}. \tag{77}
\]
After division by \(\sqrt C\), the summands are uniformly infinitesimal.  A third-order conditional characteristic-function expansion has total remainder \(O(C^{-1/2})\), uniformly over \(P\).  Hence (75)--(77) derive the triangular-array Gaussian approximation from the primitive design.

The empirical covariance is diagonal and, on the regular branch,
\[
\widehat\Sigma_{C,kk}^{(K)}
=\frac{C}{C_k^2}\sum_{c:L_c=k}\{W_c(Z_c)-\overline W_{Z_c}\}^2. \tag{78}
\]
The within-cell least-squares identity and bounded conditional variance bounds show that replacing \(\overline W_{Z_c}\) by \(\mu_{Z_c}\) changes (78) by \(o_P(1)\) uniformly.  The oracle average has mean \(\tau_k^2(P)\) and variance at most \(C_k^{-1}\).  Thus
\[
\widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}-
\operatorname{diag}(\tau_k^2(P)/a_{C,k}:k\in\mathcal K)\to_P0 \tag{79}
\]
uniformly.

For an arbitrary sequence \((P_C)\) in the nondegenerate class, \(\texttt{lem:weak-compactness-compact-laws}\) supplies a subsequence with \(P_C\Rightarrow P_\star\) on the compact schedule space.  Bounded continuity of \(W(z)\) and \(W(z)^2\) makes all cell means and variances converge.  Equations (75)--(79) then imply
\[
\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_C-U(P_C)\}\Rightarrow
N\{0,\Sigma_{CR}^{(K)}(P_\star)\},\qquad
\widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}\to_P\Sigma_{CR}^{(K)}(P_\star). \tag{80}
\]
Every pairwise contrast variance is at least \(2\underline\tau^2\).  The studentized Gaussian maximum therefore has a continuous distribution, and its quantile is continuous in covariance on the resulting compact positive-definite set.  The same subsequence contradiction as above gives uniform simultaneous pairwise coverage at level \(1-\gamma\).

On that event, the sets of policies certified strictly above or below \(k\) are subsets of the corresponding true strict-inequality sets.  Hence the inverted endpoints bracket \(r_k^-(U)\) and \(r_k^+(U)\), so \(\operatorname{Rank}_k(U)\subseteq\mathcal R_{C,k}(\gamma)\) for all \(k\), including partial ties.  The full-rank fallback in (76) can only enlarge the set.  This proves the stated uniform coverage.

semantic_closure.statement:
Fix \(A\), \(M<\infty\), and a compact set of representative local directions whose quotient norms are at most \(M\).  Under \(\mathsf B(p)\), use an independent pilot of size \(m_C\to\infty\) with \(m_C/C\to0\) to estimate \(\widehat\Sigma_{C,A}\), snap it outward to a prespecified rational covariance partition, compute the corresponding compact certificate selector \(\delta_{\varepsilon,A}\), and apply that selector to the calibrated estimator from the remaining clusters.  Uniformly over \(p\in\Delta_K\) and over that compact local set,
\[
\limsup_{C\to\infty}\left\{\sqrt C\,\mathbb E_{(Q^B_{\bar P_{C,h},p})^{\otimes C}}
\left[\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_{\delta_{\varepsilon,A}}(\bar P_{C,h})\right]
-U_\varepsilon(v_A,(Bp)_A)\right\}\leq0.
\]
There is a diagonal choice \(\varepsilon_C\downarrow0\), with pilot fraction still vanishing and pilot size diverging, whose Gaussian risk converges uniformly to \(G_{A,M}(v_A,(Bp)_A)\).  The uniformity over \(p\) uses the primitive bound \(\min_{p\in\Delta_K}(Bp)_k=\min_{\ell\in\mathcal K}B_{k\ell}>0\) for every active \(k\).  When this result is invoked in the hierarchical construction, it holds simultaneously over the finitely many retained subsets \(S\subseteq A\).  Global adaptation over every candidate policy is obtained by taking \(A=\mathcal K\), for which Bernoulli positivity supplies positive information for every candidate.
semantic_closure.justification: This turns the compact Gaussian receipt into an implementable calibrated Bernoulli rule with uniform nominal-label control.
semantic_closure.gap: Gaussian certificates require a separate bounded-score, cell-positivity, and covariance-snapping transfer to the exact-hit experiment.
semantic_closure.consumer: It implements the certified fixed-face selector under Bernoulli saturation labels.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Let \(m_C\to\infty\) and \(m_C/C\to0\).  The exact-hit factorization gives, uniformly over \(p\in\Delta_K\),
\[
\Pr_p(Z=z)=\frac{(Bp)_k}{M_k}\geq
\frac{\min_{\ell\in\mathcal K}B_{k\ell}}{M_k}>0,
\qquad z\in\mathcal S_k. \tag{81}
\]
Boundedness, cellwise Chebyshev inequalities, and a finite union bound make pilot cell means, second moments, hit rates, and \(\widehat\Sigma_{C,A}\) uniformly consistent.  Active nondegeneracy and (81) put the quotient covariance in a compact uniformly positive-definite set.

Fix \(\varepsilon\), cover that set by the finite rational terminal cells from \(\texttt{thm:gaussian-finite-certificate}\), and use the recorded boundary convention.  Conditional on the pilot, the main records are independent of the selected represented rule.  The bounded characteristic-function expansion in \(\texttt{thm:efficient-exact-hit-bernoulli}\) and the local mean calculation in \(\texttt{thm:target-tangent-lan-bernoulli}\) are uniform over \(p\) by (81) and over the compact local set.  Each represented selector has finitely many Gaussian-null action boundaries.  Conditional weak convergence therefore gives its Gaussian risk, uniformly over the finite receipt family.  The bounded tilt also gives
\[
\sqrt C\{\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_a(\bar P_{C,h})\}
=\max_{k\in A}h_k-h_a+o(1) \tag{82}
\]
uniformly.  Since \(\sqrt C/\sqrt{C-m_C}\to1\), the pilot does not change the limit.  The certificate upper bound and (82) prove the displayed limit superior.

For tolerance \(1/j\), choose a deterministic threshold after which pilot and main-sample errors are at most \(1/j\), and let \(j=j(C)\uparrow\infty\) slowly.  Then the pilot size diverges, its fraction vanishes, and the certificate gap implies uniform convergence to \(G_{A,M}\).  There are finitely many \(S\subseteq A\), so the largest of their error terms still vanishes.  Taking \(A=\mathcal K\) and using (81) yields the stated all-candidate scope.

semantic_closure.statement: Under \(\mathsf B(p)\), \(\phi_k^B\in L^2_0(Q^B_{P_0,p})\) is the canonical gradient of \(U_k\), with variance \(\tau_k^2/q_k\) and zero covariance across distinct slices. The full calibrated vector satisfies \[\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_C-U(P_0)\}\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma_B^{(K)}),\qquad \widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}\to_P\Sigma_B^{(K)}.\] Its active restriction has covariance \(\Sigma_{B,A}=(\Sigma_B^{(K)})_{AA}\).
semantic_closure.justification: This derives the full-vector calibrated score and primitive Bernoulli CLT that underlie the headline mechanism comparison.
semantic_closure.gap: HanOwusuShin2026 Appendix-B Eq. (S1) is a nominal-label Horvitz--Thompson construction rather than the pooled assignment-calibrated canonical gradient.
semantic_closure.consumer: Every realized exact hit can contribute to full-menu welfare estimation and active-face policy selection.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Put \(g_z=\Pr(Z=z)\).  By \(\texttt{lem:exact-hit-factorization}\), \(g_z=q_k/M_k>0\) for \(z\in\mathcal S_k\).  In the saturated conditional-outcome model, a regular submodel has a centered score \(s_z(Y(z))\) in cell \(z\); the known assignment law has zero score.  Differentiation of the target functional gives
\[
 \dot U_k(s)=\frac1{M_k}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}
 \mathbb E_{P_0}\!\left[(W(z)-\mu_z)s_z(Y(z))\right]. \tag{10}
\]
For \(\phi_k^B=q_k^{-1}\mathbf1\{Z\in\mathcal S_k\}(W(Z)-\mu_Z)\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{Q^B_{P_0,p}}(\phi_k^Bs_Z)
 =\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\frac{q_k/M_k}{q_k}
 \mathbb E_{P_0}\!\left[(W(z)-\mu_z)s_z(Y(z))\right]
 =\dot U_k(s). \tag{11}
\]
The coordinate is conditionally centered and bounded by \(q_k^{-1}\), hence lies in \(L_0^2\), and it belongs to the direct sum of the conditional tangent spaces.  Equations (10)--(11) make it the unique tangent-space Riesz representer, hence the canonical gradient.  Its covariance is
\[
 \mathbb E(\phi_k^B)^2
 =\frac1{q_k^2}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\frac{q_k}{M_k}
 \operatorname{Var}_{P_0}\{W(z)\}=\frac{\tau_k^2}{q_k}, \tag{12}
\]
and \(\phi_j^B\phi_k^B=0\) pointwise for \(j\ne k\), because the slices are disjoint.

For a target cell \(z\), the law of large numbers gives \(N_z/C\to_Pg_z\).  On \(N_z>0\), the exact ratio identity followed by Slutsky's theorem yields
\[
 \sqrt C(\overline W_z-\mu_z)
 =\frac1{g_z\sqrt C}\sum_{c=1}^C\mathbf1\{Z_c=z\}
   \{W_c(z)-\mu_z\}+o_P(1). \tag{13}
\]
The fallback is negligible because \(\Pr(N_z=0)=(1-g_z)^C\leq e^{-Cg_z}\).  Averaging (13) over each finite slice and using \(M_kg_z=q_k\) gives jointly
\[
 \sqrt C\{\widetilde U_C-U(P_0)\}
 =C^{-1/2}\sum_{c=1}^C(\phi_1^B(O_c),\ldots,\phi_K^B(O_c))'+o_P(1). \tag{14}
\]
The summands are iid, centered, and bounded.  For fixed \(a\in\mathbb R^K\), Taylor expansion of their characteristic function gives
\[
 \left(1-\frac{a'\Sigma_B^{(K)}a}{2C}+O(C^{-3/2})\right)^C
 \longrightarrow e^{-a'\Sigma_B^{(K)}a/2}. \tag{15}
\]
The Cram\'er--Wold device proves the asserted joint normal limit.

On the regular branch define
\[
 \widehat q_k=C^{-1}\sum_c\mathbf1\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\},\qquad
 \widehat\phi_{c,k}=\widehat q_k^{-1}\mathbf1\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}
 \{W_c(Z_c)-\overline W_{Z_c}\}.
\]
The prescribed fallback handles undefined cells.  There are finitely many cells, each count diverges in probability, and all observations lie in \([0,1]\).  Cellwise laws of large numbers and the within-cell least-squares identity imply
\[
 C^{-1}\sum_{c=1}^C\widehat\phi_c\widehat\phi_c'\to_P
 \mathbb E\{\phi^B(\phi^B)'\}=\Sigma_B^{(K)}. \tag{16}
\]
Off-diagonal empirical products vanish identically.  Restricting (14)--(16) to \(A\) proves the final assertion.

semantic_closure.statement: Fix \(k\) with \(p_k>0\), and write \(\eta_k=p_kB_{kk}\). Han--Owusu--Shin Appendix-B Eq. (S1) is exactly \[\widehat U^{HOS}_{C,k}=\frac{1}{Cp_k}\sum_{c=1}^C\mathbf 1\{L_c=k\}\frac{\gamma_k(Z_c)}{\beta_k(Z_c)}W_c(Z_c)=\frac{1}{C\eta_k}\sum_{c=1}^C\mathbf 1\{L_c=k,Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}W_c(Z_c).\] It has influence function \(\phi_k^{HOS}=\eta_k^{-1}\mathbf 1\{L=k,Z\in\mathcal S_k\}W(Z)-U_k\) and \[\operatorname{AVAR}(\widehat U^{HOS}_{C,k})=\frac{\tau_k^2+b_k^2}{\eta_k}+U_k^2\left(\frac1{\eta_k}-1\right).\] The best regular estimator in the nominal-label-\(k\) subexperiment has canonical gradient \(\phi_k^{nom}\) and efficiency bound \(\tau_k^2/\eta_k\). Therefore, whenever \(q_k>\eta_k\) and \(\tau_k^2>0\), \[\frac{\tau_k^2}{q_k}<\frac{\tau_k^2}{p_kB_{kk}}\leq\operatorname{AVAR}(\widehat U^{HOS}_{C,k}).\] If \(b_k^2>0\), assignment-cell calibration within the nominal subexperiment is itself strictly more efficient than Eq. (S1), apart from the additional Horvitz--Thompson participation term displayed above.
semantic_closure.justification: This makes the closest same-target comparison exact at the estimator, influence-function, and variance levels.
semantic_closure.gap: HanOwusuShin2026 Appendix B proves unbiasedness of Eq. (S1) but does not derive the pooled efficient bound or separate its cell-heterogeneity and Horvitz--Thompson participation losses.
semantic_closure.consumer: Analysts can quantify both the cross-label gain and the additional gain from assignment-cell calibration over the published estimator.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
For \(z\in\mathcal S_k\),
\[
 \frac{\gamma_k(z)}{\beta_k(z)}
 =\frac{M_k^{-1}}{\pi_k^{m_k}(1-\pi_k)^{n-m_k}}=\frac1{B_{kk}}. \tag{22}
\]
Substitution in the Horvitz--Thompson formula, with \(\eta_k=p_kB_{kk}>0\), proves the displayed estimator identity.  Its iid summand has mean \(U_k\), because conditional assignment is uniform on \(\mathcal S_k\), and hence its exact influence coordinate is
\(\phi_k^{HOS}=\eta_k^{-1}\mathbf1\{L=k,Z\in\mathcal S_k\}W(Z)-U_k\).  Furthermore
\[
 \mathbb E\{W(Z)^2\mid L=k,Z\in\mathcal S_k\}
 =\tau_k^2+M_k^{-1}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\mu_z^2
 =\tau_k^2+b_k^2+U_k^2.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\phi_k^{HOS})
 =\frac{\tau_k^2+b_k^2}{\eta_k}+U_k^2(\eta_k^{-1}-1). \tag{23}
\]
In the nominal-label target-hit subexperiment, each \(z\in\mathcal S_k\) occurs with probability \(\eta_k/M_k\).  The tangent-space calculation (10)--(12), with \(q_k\) replaced by \(\eta_k\), proves that \(\phi_k^{nom}\) is canonical and has variance \(\tau_k^2/\eta_k\).  Since \(b_k^2,U_k^2\geq0\) and \(0<\eta_k\leq1\), (23) is at least this bound.  If \(q_k>\eta_k\) and \(\tau_k^2>0\), positivity permits division and gives
\[
 \tau_k^2/q_k<\tau_k^2/\eta_k\leq\operatorname{Var}(\phi_k^{HOS}).
\]
Finally \(b_k^2>0\) makes the cell-heterogeneity term \(b_k^2/\eta_k\) strictly positive, independently of the nonnegative participation term.

semantic_closure.statement:
For every fixed \(C\), \(p\), and bounded target-only loss \(\mathcal L\), regime \(\mathsf B(p)\) satisfies
\[
\inf_{\delta\in\mathfrak D_C}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[\mathcal L(U,\delta(\mathcal E_{C,B}^{\mathrm{full}}(p)))]
=
\inf_{\delta\in\mathfrak D_C}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[\mathcal L(U,\delta(\mathcal E_{C,B}^{\mathrm{hit}}(p)))].
\]
The equality persists after deleting \(L_c\) conditional on every realized target assignment.  More generally, the same equality holds when the displayed finite deployment action space and its rule class are replaced by any standard-Borel decision space and all measurable randomized rules, provided the loss is bounded and depends on the schedule law only through \(U\).  This includes the ranking action of Han--Owusu--Shin.  It holds for rules observing the entire outcome vector because the reverse inequality fixes every nontarget assignment marginal at a known distribution and replaces the unidentified schedule coupling by the product of its assignment-specific marginals.
semantic_closure.justification: This all-rule equality isolates exactly which Bernoulli observations can carry worst-case information about the target.
semantic_closure.gap: No named comparator proves a finite-sample all-measurable-rule deletion equivalence over unrestricted assignment-specific schedule marginals.
semantic_closure.consumer: It licenses the full-experiment local minimax lower bound without a spillover response model.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Let \(R_{\mathrm{full}}\) and \(R_{\mathrm{hit}}\) denote the two minimax risks.  The hit record is a measurable image of the full record, so every hit-rule lifts to a full-rule and
\[
 R_{\mathrm{full}}\leq R_{\mathrm{hit}}. \tag{4}
\]
For each assignment \(z\), write \(F_z\) for the marginal law of \((Y_j(z))_{j=1}^n\) under \(P\).  Because \([0,1]^n\) is standard Borel and \(\mathcal Z_n\) is finite, every collection \((F_z:z\in\mathcal Z_n)\) is realized by the legal product schedule law \(\bigotimes_zF_z\).  Fix known laws \(F_z^0\) off \(\bigcup_k\mathcal S_k\), and let \(\mathcal P_0\) contain the product schedule laws having those nontarget marginals and arbitrary target marginals.  This restriction leaves unrestricted both the possible target vector \(U\) and the target-hit observed laws.

Given any randomized full-data rule \(\delta\), construct a hit-data rule \(\delta^0\) by conditionally drawing every omitted nontarget outcome vector from the known law \(F_{Z_c}^0\), independently across clusters, and applying \(\delta\) to the completed record.  Existence of this parameter-free simulation kernel follows from the standard-Borel condition.  For every \(P\in\mathcal P_0\), the completed record has exactly its full-experiment law, and hence
\[
 \mathbb E_P\mathcal L(U,\delta^0)=\mathbb E_P\mathcal L(U,\delta). \tag{5}
\]
Since \(\mathcal P_0\subseteq\mathcal P\) and its target marginals exhaust the reduced parameter space,
\[
 \sup_P\mathbb E_P\mathcal L(U,\delta)
 \geq\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_0}\mathbb E_P\mathcal L(U,\delta)
 =\sup_P\mathbb E_P\mathcal L(U,\delta^0)
 \geq R_{\mathrm{hit}}. \tag{6}
\]
Taking the infimum over \(\delta\) and combining (4)--(6) proves equality for every bounded target-only loss on an arbitrary standard-Borel action space.

For \(z\in\mathcal S_k\), \(\texttt{lem:exact-hit-factorization}\) supplies the known kernel
\[
 \Pr(L_c=\ell\mid Z_c=z)=p_\ell B_{k\ell}/q_k. \tag{7}
\]
It is parameter-free and well defined because \(q_k>0\).  Thus a label-observing rule can be reproduced after label deletion by simulating (7), while forgetting the label gives the reverse comparison.  This proves label deletion.  A ranking vector is finite and therefore standard Borel, so the Han--Owusu--Shin ranking action is included.

semantic_closure.statement: Under \(\mathsf B(p)\), \(\widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}\to_P\Sigma_B^{(K)}\), and \[\liminf_{C\to\infty}\inf_{P:\min_k\tau_k^2(P)\geq\underline\tau^2}\Pr_P\{\operatorname{Rank}_k(U)\subseteq\mathcal R_{C,k}(\gamma)\text{ for every }k\in\mathcal K\}\geq1-\gamma.\] The assertion is uniform over partial ties. The full-rank empty-cell fallback is always defined, and its activation probability is at most \(\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}M_k\exp(-Cq_k/M_k)\).
semantic_closure.justification: This states the correct set-valued rank target at ties.
semantic_closure.gap: MogstadRomanoShaikhWilhelm2024 begins from a joint approximation and does not derive calibrated random-hit scores.
semantic_closure.consumer: Bernoulli saturation studies obtain simultaneous winner and rank uncertainty.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix \(p\in\Delta_K\) and \(0<\gamma<1\).  Every \(B_{k\ell}>0\), hence \(q_k>0\), and \(\texttt{lem:exact-hit-factorization}\) gives, for \(z\in\mathcal S_k\),
\[
r_z:=\Pr(Z_c=z)=q_k/M_k>0. \tag{66}
\]
Set \(\widehat r_z=N_z/C\) and
\[
A_{C,z}=C^{-1}\sum_{c=1}^C\mathbf1\{Z_c=z\}\{W_c(z)-\mu_z\}.
\]
Boundedness gives uniformly in \(P\)
\[
\mathbb EA_{C,z}^2\leq C^{-1},\qquad
\mathbb E(\widehat r_z-r_z)^2\leq C^{-1}. \tag{67}
\]
Since there are finitely many positive-probability target cells, Chebyshev and a union bound imply
\[
\max_z|A_{C,z}|=O_P(C^{-1/2}),\quad
\max_z|\widehat r_z-r_z|=O_P(C^{-1/2}),\quad
\min_z\widehat r_z\geq\tfrac12\min_zr_z
\]
with probability tending to one, uniformly in \(P\).  On that event, expanding every cell ratio gives
\[
\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_C-U(P)\}
=C^{-1/2}\sum_{c=1}^C\xi_c(P)+o_P(1),\qquad
\xi_{c,k}=q_k^{-1}\mathbf1\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}
\{W_c(Z_c)-\mu_{Z_c}\}. \tag{68}
\]
The remainder is \(o_P(1)\) after scaling because it is a finite sum of products of the two \(O_P(C^{-1/2})\) errors in (67).  This is the canonical-gradient expansion in \(\texttt{thm:efficient-exact-hit-bernoulli}\).

Conditioning on cells gives
\[
\mathbb E\xi_{c,k}=0,\qquad
\mathbb E\xi_{c,k}^2=\tau_k^2(P)/q_k,\qquad
\mathbb E(\xi_{c,j}\xi_{c,k})=0\quad(j\ne k). \tag{69}
\]
Thus the covariance is \(\Sigma_B^{(K)}(P)\).  To prove uniformity, take any sequence \((P_C)\) with \(\min_k\tau_k^2(P_C)\geq\underline\tau^2\).  The schedule space \([0,1]^{n\times\mathcal Z_n}\) is compact metric, so \(\texttt{lem:weak-compactness-compact-laws}\) supplies from every subsequence a further subsequence with \(P_C\Rightarrow P_\infty\).  The coordinate maps \(W(z)\) and \(W(z)^2\) are bounded continuous, whence
\[
\Sigma_B^{(K)}(P_C)\longrightarrow\Sigma_B^{(K)}(P_\infty)=:\Sigma_\infty. \tag{70}
\]
The limit is positive definite by the variance lower bound.  For fixed \(a\), \(a'\xi_c(P_C)\) is uniformly bounded, so
\[
\mathbb E_{P_C}e^{\mathrm ia'\xi_c(P_C)/\sqrt C}
=1-\frac{a'\Sigma_B^{(K)}(P_C)a}{2C}+O(C^{-3/2}), \tag{71}
\]
uniformly along the sequence.  Independence, (68), and (70)--(71) give
\[
\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_C-U(P_C)\}\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma_\infty). \tag{72}
\]

For studentization, on the regular branch put
\[
\widehat\xi_{c,k}=\widehat q_k^{-1}\mathbf1\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}
\{W_c(Z_c)-\overline W_{Z_c}\}.
\]
The within-cell identity
\[
\sum_{c:Z_c=z}(W_c(z)-\overline W_z)^2
=\sum_{c:Z_c=z}(W_c(z)-\mu_z)^2-N_z(\overline W_z-\mu_z)^2
\]
and (67) show uniformly that centering by \(\overline W_z\) instead of \(\mu_z\) changes empirical second moments by \(o_P(1)\).  Bounded laws of large numbers and \(\widehat q_k\to q_k\) then give
\[
\widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}-\Sigma_B^{(K)}(P)\to_P0 \tag{73}
\]
uniformly over the displayed class.

Let \(e_{ij}=e_i-e_j\), define
\[
T_C=\max_{i<j}\frac{\sqrt C|e_{ij}'(\widetilde U_C-U)|}
{(e_{ij}'\widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}e_{ij})^{1/2}},
\]
and let \(c_C(\gamma)\) be the conditional \((1-\gamma)\)-quantile of the analogous Gaussian maximum with covariance \(\widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}\).  Every limiting contrast variance is at least \(\underline\tau^2(q_i^{-1}+q_j^{-1})>0\).  Hence (72)--(73) imply
\[
T_C\Rightarrow\max_{i<j}\frac{|e_{ij}'G_\infty|}
{(e_{ij}'\Sigma_\infty e_{ij})^{1/2}},\qquad G_\infty\sim N(0,\Sigma_\infty). \tag{74}
\]
This Gaussian maximum has a continuous distribution: its contrast vector has a positive density on the \((K-1)\)-dimensional contrast space and max-norm spheres have Lebesgue measure zero.  Thus plug-in Gaussian quantiles are continuous and simultaneous pairwise coverage tends to \(1-\gamma\).  If uniform coverage failed, a violating sequence and the weakly convergent subsequence above would contradict (74).  This proves the displayed uniform liminf.

On simultaneous contrast coverage, a policy certified above \(k\) is truly above it, and a policy certified below \(k\) is truly below it.  Therefore the inverted lower rank endpoint is at most \(r_k^-(U)\) and its upper endpoint is at least \(r_k^+(U)\), simultaneously for all \(k\).  This deterministic implication uses no separation and covers all partial ties.  Finally
\[
\Pr(N_z=0)=(1-q_k/M_k)^C\leq e^{-Cq_k/M_k}.
\]
A union bound gives the stated fallback probability.  The fallback returns all ranks, so it cannot reduce coverage.

semantic_closure.statement:
Let \(A=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_kU_k(P_0)\), with \(|A|\geq2\), and suppose every policy in \(A^c\) is separated below the tied active welfare.  For every representative \(h\in\mathbb R^A\), including its common-shift component, the path \(\bar P_{C,h}=\bar P_{C^{-1/2},h}\) satisfies \(Q^B_{\bar P_0,p}=Q^B_{P_0,p}\), \(dU_k(\bar P_{t,h})/dt|_{t=0}=h_k\), and
\[
\log\frac{d(Q^B_{\bar P_{C,h},p})^{\otimes C}}{d(Q^B_{P_0,p})^{\otimes C}}
=h^{\prime}\Delta_C^B-\frac12h^{\prime}I_Bh+o_{(Q^B_{P_0,p})^{\otimes C}}(1),
\qquad \Delta_C^B\Rightarrow N(0,I_B),
\]
with \(\dot\ell_k^B\in L^2_0(Q^B_{P_0,p})\) and \(I_B=\operatorname{diag}(q_k/\tau_k^2:k\in A)\).  Under \(\bar P_{C,h}\),
\[
\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_{C,A}-U_A(P_0)\}\Rightarrow
N\{h,\Sigma_{B,A}\}.
\]
For every measurable randomized rule sequence \(\delta_C\) and every \(M<\infty\),
\[
\liminf_{C\to\infty}\sup_{h\in\mathbb R^A:\ \lVert[h]\rVert_A\leq M}
\sqrt C\,\mathbb E_{(Q^B_{\bar P_{C,h},p})^{\otimes C}}
\left[\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_{\delta_C}(\bar P_{C,h})\right]
\geq G_{A,M}(\tau_A^2,q_A).
\]
Moreover \(G_{A,M}\uparrow G_A\) as \(M\to\infty\).  The same lower bounds hold for rules observing the full Bernoulli experiment by nuisance deletion.
semantic_closure.justification: The explicit full target score and quotient reduction produce an all-rule lower experiment without treating common welfare as known.
semantic_closure.gap: HiranoPorter2009 supplies general local-limit architecture, not this nuisance-deleted exact-hit score or its common-location quotient.
semantic_closure.consumer: It proves that nontarget observations cannot erase Bernoulli mechanism loss under unrestricted schedules.
semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Only one assignment is observed from each schedule.  Consequently \(P_0\) and \(\bar P_0=\bigotimes_zP_{0,z}\) induce the same one-cluster observed law, so \(Q^B_{\bar P_0,p}=Q^B_{P_0,p}\).  The iid schedule, label, schedule-independence, and unit-randomization assumptions make the records independent and give the target-cell probabilities in \(\texttt{lem:exact-hit-factorization}\).

Fix an arbitrary \(h\in\mathbb R^A\), with no restriction on its common-shift component.  For \(z\in\mathcal S_k\), bounded-support exponential tilting gives score
\[
 h_k\{W(z)-\mu_z\}/\tau_k^2
\]
and, by differentiation under a bounded integral,
\[
 \left.\frac d{dt}\mathbb E_{P_{t,h,z}}W(z)\right|_{t=0}
 =\frac{h_k}{\tau_k^2}\operatorname{Var}_{P_0}\{W(z)\}. \tag{36}
\]
Division is valid by \(\tau_k^2\geq\underline\tau^2>0\).  Averaging (36) over \(\mathcal S_k\) gives
\[
 \left.\frac d{dt}U_k(\bar P_{t,h})\right|_{t=0}
 =\frac{h_k}{M_k\tau_k^2}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}
 \operatorname{Var}_{P_0}\{W(z)\}=h_k. \tag{37}
\]
The observed score is \(\dot\ell_k^B\).  It is centered and bounded, and disjointness of the slices gives
\[
 \mathbb E_0(\dot\ell_j^B\dot\ell_k^B)
 =\mathbf1\{j=k\}\frac{q_k}{M_k\tau_k^4}
 \sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\operatorname{Var}_{P_0}\{W(z)\}
 =\mathbf1\{j=k\}\frac{q_k}{\tau_k^2}. \tag{38}
\]
Thus the score covariance is \(I_B\), including the common-shift score \(\sum_k\dot\ell_k^B\).

The early four-node check follows directly from (38).  If the four count-one welfare bits have mean \(1/2\), then \(\tau_1^2=1/4\), information is \(4q_1\), and calibrated influence variance is \(1/(4q_1)\).  For cell means \((4/5,4/5,1/5,1/5)\), every cell variance is \(4/25\), so information is \(25q_1/4\) and influence variance is \(4/(25q_1)\).  In both cases the exact-hit multiplier is \(q_1\).  The empty-cell fallback has finite-sample bias
\[
 \frac1{M_k}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}(1/2-\mu_z)
 \left(1-\frac{q_k}{M_k}\right)^C,
\]
which is exponentially small because \(q_k/M_k>0\); no finite-sample unbiasedness is used.

Because \(0\leq W\leq1\), Taylor's theorem for the log moment-generating function gives, uniformly for \(a\) in a fixed neighborhood of zero,
\[
 \Lambda_{z,k}(a)=\frac{a^2}{2}\operatorname{Var}_{P_0}\{W(z)\}+O(|a|^3). \tag{39}
\]
Substitute \(a=C^{-1/2}h_k/\tau_k^2\), sum over clusters, and use the bounded law of large numbers for assignment-cell frequencies.  The linear term is \(h'\Delta_C^B\), (38)--(39) give \(-h'I_Bh/2+o_P(1)\), and the summed cubic remainder is \(O(C^{-1/2}\max_k|h_k|^3)\) on each compact set of representatives.  The summands of \(\Delta_C^B\) are iid, centered, bounded vectors with covariance \(I_B\), so their characteristic functions yield \(\Delta_C^B\Rightarrow N(0,I_B)\).  This proves the displayed LAN expansion.

Equations (37)--(39), together with the asymptotic linear expansion in \(\texttt{thm:efficient-exact-hit-bernoulli}\), give under \(\bar P_{C,h}\), uniformly on compact representative sets, the following result: multiplying the joint null characteristic function by the displayed likelihood ratio shifts its linear exponent by \(h\) and leaves its quadratic covariance exponent unchanged, so
\[
 \sqrt C\{\widetilde U_{C,A}-U_A(P_0)\}\Rightarrow
 N\{h,\Sigma_{B,A}\}. \tag{40}
\]
For the decision lower bound, take any finite collection of representatives with \(\lVert[h]\rVert_A\leq M\) and any finite prior.  The LAN likelihood ratios and (37) verify the premises of \(\texttt{lem:lan-finite-prior-lower-bound}\); bounded scores give uniform integrability.  Thus the limiting maximal scaled causal regret is at least that prior's Bayes risk in the full Gaussian shift experiment.

To retain the unknown common location, tensor any finite quotient prior with a uniform grid of shifts \(c\mathbf1_A\), \(-T\leq c\leq T\).  Gaussian total-variation continuity makes the mesh error vanish, and the shift grid's boundary-to-volume ratio vanishes as \(T\to\infty\).  The resulting averaged rule is location invariant.  On the compact quotient ball, the loss is bounded and Lipschitz and Gaussian translation is continuous in total variation, so all selector risks have a common modulus; an arbitrarily fine finite quotient grid therefore approximates the supremum risk uniformly over selectors.  On such a finite grid, the orthonormal-basis diagonalization in \(\texttt{lem:gaussian-quotient-reduction}\) makes the attainable finite risk-vector set compact and convex.  Separating it from a strictly lower orthant gives nonnegative separating coefficients summing to one, namely a finite prior, and proves that the finite-grid minimax value is the supremum of its finite-prior Bayes values.  Letting the quotient mesh vanish, then the shift mesh vanish and \(T\to\infty\), and applying the quotient reduction gives \(G_{A,M}(\tau_A^2,q_A)\).  The fixed baseline gap makes every inactive action asymptotically dominated.  The quotient lemma also gives \(G_{A,M}\uparrow G_A\), while \(\texttt{thm:nuisance-deletion-bernoulli}\) transfers the lower bound to full-record rules.

For homogeneity, write \(X=h+\operatorname{diag}(v_k/(sr_k))^{1/2}Z\), set \(\widetilde X=\sqrt sX\) and \(\widetilde h=\sqrt sh\), and use the bijection \(\widetilde\delta(\widetilde x)=\delta(\widetilde x/\sqrt s)\). \[
 G_A(v_A,sr_A)=s^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,r_A). \tag{29}
\]
If \(r'_k\geq r_k>0\), add independent coordinatewise Gaussian noise of variance \(v_k/r_k-v_k/r'_k\) to the rate-\(r'_A\) observation.  The resulting law is the rate-\(r_A\) experiment.  Composition with this parameter-free kernel proves
\[
G_A(v_A,r'_A)\leq G_A(v_A,r_A). \tag{30}
\]
Applying (29)--(30) to \((1-\xi)r_A\leq r'_A\leq(1+\xi)r_A\) proves the stated two-sided modulus.

Finiteness follows from the largest-coordinate rule.  If \(i\) is best and \(d_j=h_i-h_j\), then
\[
R(h,\delta_{\max})\leq\sum_{j\ne i}d_j

\leq\kappa\sum_{j\ne i}\sqrt{v_i/r_i+v_j/r_j}<\infty. \tag{31}
\]
For positivity, restrict to two arms \(i\ne j\), send all other means to \(-H\), and place equal prior mass on two quotient points having gap \(d\) with opposite signs.  In the quotient experiment, the sign test has error \(\Phi(-d/a_{ij})\), where \(a_{ij}^2=v_i/r_i+v_j/r_j\), and Bayes regret \(d\Phi(-d/a_{ij})\).  Letting \(H\to\infty\) and maximizing at \(d=a_{ij}x\) gives
\[
G_A(v_A,r_A)\geq\kappa a_{ij}>0. \tag{32}
\]
If an action-relevant \(r_i^{(m)}\downarrow0\), choose any other action-relevant \(j\); the right side of (32) diverges.  Thus every positive sequence approaching such a boundary has limit inferior \(+\infty\), and the stipulated lower-semicontinuous boundary value is \(+\infty\).

semantic_closure.proof_tex:
Fix \(c\), \(k\), \(\ell\), and \(z\in\mathcal S_k\).  The coordinate sum of \(z\) is \(m_k\).  By \(\texttt{ass:bernoulli-label-iid}\), \(\texttt{ass:bernoulli-label-schedule-independence}\), and \(\texttt{ass:bernoulli-units}\),
\[
 \Pr(L_c=\ell,Z_c=z)
 =p_\ell\pi_\ell^{m_k}(1-\pi_\ell)^{n-m_k}
 =\frac{p_\ell B_{k\ell}}{M_k}. \tag{1}
\]
Summing (1) over \(\ell\) and using \(q=Bp\) gives
\[
 \Pr(Z_c=z)=\frac1{M_k}\sum_{\ell=1}^Kp_\ell B_{k\ell}=\frac{q_k}{M_k}. \tag{2}
\]
Every \(B_{k\ell}\) is positive because \(1\leq m_k\leq n-1\) and \(0<\pi_\ell<1\).  Since \(p\in\Delta_K\), at least one \(p_\ell\) is positive, whence \(q_k>0\).  Division by (2) is therefore valid, and Bayes' identity yields
\[
 \Pr(L_c=\ell\mid Z_c=z)=\frac{p_\ell B_{k\ell}}{q_k}. \tag{3}
\]
The right side of (2) is constant over the \(M_k\) elements of \(\mathcal S_k\).  Hence \(\Pr(Z_c\in\mathcal S_k)=q_k\) and \(Z_c\) is conditionally uniform on that slice.  Distinct \(m_k\)'s make the slices pairwise disjoint.  Finally the cluster labels, schedules, and conditional randomizations are independent across \(c\); thus the indicators of the \(K\) disjoint hit events and their complement are iid categorical with probabilities \((q_1,\ldots,q_K,1-\sum_kq_k)\).  Their totals have the asserted multinomial law.

Write \(X=h+\xi\), independently generate \(E\sim N(0,\Sigma)\), and put
\[
X^{\mathrm s}=X+\sqrt{(1-\lambda)/\lambda}\,E,\qquad
X^{\mathrm d}=X-\sqrt{\lambda/(1-\lambda)}\,E. \tag{59}
\]
Then
\[
X^{\mathrm s}\sim N(h,\Sigma/\lambda),\qquad
X^{\mathrm d}\sim N(h,\Sigma/(1-\lambda)),\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}(X^{\mathrm s},X^{\mathrm d})=0. \tag{60}
\]
Joint Gaussianity makes the two observations independent.  Retain
\[
\widehat S=\{i:X_i^{\mathrm s}\geq\max_jX_j^{\mathrm s}-T\}. \tag{61}
\]
Conditional on \(\widehat S=S\), feed \(\sqrt{1-\lambda}\,X_S^{\mathrm d}\) to the compact selector.  Its covariance is \(\Sigma_{SS}\), its mean is \(\sqrt{1-\lambda}h_S\), and the construction is measurable and location invariant.

Let \(b\) maximize \(h\), set \(d_i=h_b-h_i\), and write \(\xi^{\mathrm s}=X^{\mathrm s}-h\).  Each screening contrast has standard deviation at most \(a_\lambda=\sqrt{2/\lambda}\bar\sigma\).  Since
\[
\Phi(-x)\leq\varphi(x)/x\qquad(x>0), \tag{62}
\]
if \(b\notin\widehat S\), summing over a maximizing screening coordinate gives deletion loss at most
\[
\frac{(d-1)a_\lambda}{\sqrt{2\pi}}
e^{-T^2/(2a_\lambda^2)}. \tag{63}
\]
If retained \(i,j\) have true gap \(D>2T\), then the opposite screening-noise contrast is at least \(D-T\geq D/2\); (62) gives
\[
D\Pr\{i,j\text{ retained}\}
\leq\frac{2a_\lambda}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-T^2/(2a_\lambda^2)}. \tag{64}
\]
The range of a bad retained set is bounded by the sum of its oriented pairwise gaps.  Summing (63)--(64) over fewer than \(d^2\) indices is at most the displayed tail term.

Otherwise the true range in \(S=\widehat S\) is at most \(2T\), and therefore
\[
\lVert[\sqrt{1-\lambda}h_S]\rVert_S
\leq2\sqrt{1-\lambda}T\sqrt{|S|-1}\leq M_S. \tag{65}
\]
Independence means conditioning on the screen does not alter the decision law.  The scaled conditional regret is at most \(G_{S,M_S}+\eta\); undoing the scale multiplies it by \((1-\lambda)^{-1/2}\).  Averaging over the partition by retained subsets costs their maximum, not their sum.  Combining (58), (63)--(65) proves the bound.  The constants are uniform on compact positive-variance cells and over the finite subsets \(S\subseteq A\).  No arm outside the declared \(A\) enters; global adaptation therefore requires \(A=\mathcal K\) and positive information for each candidate.

semantic_closure.statement: The set of Borel probability laws on a compact metric space is compact for the topology of weak convergence.
semantic_closure.proof_tex: Let \(S\) be a compact metric space.  Every family of Borel probability laws on \(S\) is uniformly tight, because \(S\) itself is a compact set having probability one under every such law.  By Prohorov's theorem (\texttt{vanDerVaart1998}, Section 2.4), the family is relatively compact for weak convergence.  The class of probability laws is weakly closed: weak limits preserve nonnegativity and preserve total mass because the constant function \(1\) is bounded and continuous.  Therefore the set of Borel probability laws on \(S\) is weakly compact.

semantic_closure.statement:
When \(K=2\) and \(A=\mathcal K\), the quotient statistic is \(X_1-X_2\), and for positive rates
\[
G_A(v_A,r_A)=\kappa\sqrt{\frac{v_1}{r_1}+\frac{v_2}{r_2}},
\]
attained by selecting policy one exactly when \(X_1-X_2\geq0\).  Consequently the optimized exact-count share is
\[
\alpha_1^\star=\frac{\sqrt{v_1}}{\sqrt{v_1}+\sqrt{v_2}}.
\]
For Bernoulli labels, \(t^\star\) minimizes \(F_v(t)\).  If \(B_{11}>B_{12}\) and \(B_{22}>B_{21}\), then \(t^\star=0\) exactly when
\[
\frac{v_1}{v_2}\leq\frac{(B_{22}-B_{21})B_{12}^2}{(B_{11}-B_{12})B_{22}^2},
\]
and \(t^\star=1\) exactly when
\[
\frac{v_1}{v_2}\geq\frac{(B_{22}-B_{21})B_{11}^2}{(B_{11}-B_{12})B_{21}^2};
\]
otherwise it is the unique interior value
\[
t^\star=
\frac{B_{22}\sqrt{v_1(B_{11}-B_{12})/[v_2(B_{22}-B_{21})]}-B_{12}}
{(B_{11}-B_{12})+(B_{22}-B_{21})\sqrt{v_1(B_{11}-B_{12})/[v_2(B_{22}-B_{21})]}}.
\]
For \(n=4\), \((\pi_1,\pi_2)=(1/4,1/2)\), and \(v_1=v_2\),
\[
B=\begin{pmatrix}27/64&1/4\\27/128&3/8\end{pmatrix},\qquad
t^\star=-80+\frac{288\sqrt{462}}{77}.
\]
Relative to optimized exact-count assignment, the exact regret ratio and cluster-count ratio are, respectively,
\[
\left(\frac{43}{54}+\frac{\sqrt{462}}{27}\right)^{1/2}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\frac{43}{54}+\frac{\sqrt{462}}{27}.
\]
They lie in \([1.26189430296,1.26189430298]\) and \([1.59237723185,1.59237723187]\), while \(t^\star\in[0.39383577842,0.39383577844]\).

semantic_closure.proof_tex:
For two arms, \(D_A=(1,-1)\).  By \(\texttt{lem:gaussian-quotient-reduction}\), the experiment reduces to
\[
 Y=X_1-X_2\sim N(d,s^2),\qquad d=h_1-h_2,\qquad
 s^2=\frac{v_1}{r_1}+\frac{v_2}{r_2}. \tag{33}
\]
Choosing arm one iff \(Y\geq0\) has regret \(|d|\Phi(-|d|/s)\), whose supremum is \(\kappa s\).  Conversely, put equal prior mass on the quotient parameters \(d=\pm sx_\star\), where \(x_\star\) maximizes \(x\Phi(-x)\).  Their likelihood-ratio rule is the sign of \(Y\), and their Bayes regret is \(sx_\star\Phi(-x_\star)=\kappa s\).  Maximum risk dominates Bayes risk, proving the exact value and rule.

For exact counts, squared risk is minimized by
\[
 f(\alpha)=\frac{v_1}{\alpha}+\frac{v_2}{1-\alpha},\qquad
 f'(\alpha)=-\frac{v_1}{\alpha^2}+\frac{v_2}{(1-\alpha)^2},\qquad
 f''(\alpha)>0.
\]
The unique stationary point, and hence the global minimizer because \(f\) diverges at both endpoints, is
\(\alpha_1^\star=\sqrt{v_1}/(\sqrt{v_1}+\sqrt{v_2})\).

For Bernoulli labels put \(a=B_{11}\), \(b=B_{12}\), \(c=B_{21}\), \(d_0=B_{22}\), \(A_0=a-b>0\), and \(D_0=d_0-c>0\).  Then
\[
F_v'(t)=-\frac{v_1A_0}{(b+A_0t)^2}+\frac{v_2D_0}{(d_0-D_0t)^2},\qquad
F_v''(t)=\frac{2v_1A_0^2}{(b+A_0t)^3}+\frac{2v_2D_0^2}{(d_0-D_0t)^3}>0. \tag{34}
\]
The signs of \(F_v'(0)\) and \(F_v'(1)\) give exactly the two endpoint inequalities in the statement.  Otherwise the unique root of \(F_v'\) is obtained by taking the positive square root and solving the resulting linear equation, giving the displayed interior formula.  Strict convexity certifies optimality.

For \(n=4\), direct binomial arithmetic gives
\[
B_{11}=27/64,\quad B_{12}=1/4,\quad B_{21}=27/128,\quad B_{22}=3/8.
\]
Substitution with \(v_1=v_2\) gives
\[
t^\star=-80+\frac{288\sqrt{462}}{77},\quad
q_1=-\frac{27}{2}+\frac{9\sqrt{462}}{14},\quad
q_2=\frac{27}{2}-\frac{27\sqrt{462}}{44},
\]
and exact simplification yields
\[
\frac14(q_1^{-1}+q_2^{-1})=\frac{43}{54}+\frac{\sqrt{462}}{27}. \tag{35}
\]
The regret ratio is the square root of (35), and the cluster-count ratio is (35).  Squaring rational endpoints to enclose \(462\), then using monotonicity of the positive arithmetic operations, gives the three outward decimal intervals stated in the theorem.

payload.honest_scope: The results concern fixed \(n\), fixed \(K\), equal cluster sizes, distinct interior rational saturations, isolated iid cluster schedules, and exact-slice welfare. Bernoulli-label and exact-count complete randomization are mutually exclusive regimes, and all scores are defined under their induced observed laws. Active-face complete-randomization results allow zero inactive shares, but full-menu central limit and rank results require every reported share to be positive. At a unique best policy first-order local regret is zero. When \(K=2\), the face game reduces to the sign rule and Neyman allocation; assignment-homogeneous slice means eliminate the calibration component but not necessarily the Horvitz--Thompson participation term in Eq. (S1). The noncompact certificate is uniform over retained subsets of a declared face and uniformly positive-definite covariance cells. Global adaptation takes \(A=\mathcal K\); Bernoulli designs range over the full nominal-label simplex because \(B\) gives positive hit rates, whereas primitive exact-count transfer is uniform only on compact subsets of the active simplex interior. A vanishing action-relevant rate is assigned the extended value \(+\infty\), not a positive-rate Gaussian formula. The Kenya design remains a prospective design consumer rather than an authorized reanalysis.

Let \(\Theta\) and \(\mathcal D\) be nonempty finite sets and let \(d\geq1\) be an integer.  Define the action simplex by \(\Delta_{\mathcal D}=\{v\in[0,1]^{\mathcal D}:\sum_{a\in\mathcal D}v_a=1\}\), and let \(\varpi=(\varpi_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta}\) be a probability mass function.  For each positive integer \(C\), let \(\mathsf E_C=(\mathsf X_C,\mathcal F_C,\{P_{C,\theta}:\theta\in\Theta\})\) be an experiment whose laws are all dominated by a reference probability measure \(P_{C,0}\) on \((\mathsf X_C,\mathcal F_C)\), and write \(L_{C,\theta}=dP_{C,\theta}/dP_{C,0}\).  Let the limit experiment be a Gaussian-shift experiment on \(\mathbb R^d\), with canonical observation \(G\), laws \(Q_\theta\) all dominated by a reference law \(Q_0\), and likelihood ratios \(L_\theta(G)=dQ_\theta/dQ_0(G)\).  Suppose that: (i) there are measurable statistics \(T_C\colon\mathsf X_C\to\mathbb R^d\) such that, under \(P_{C,0}\),
\[
 \bigl(T_C,(L_{C,\theta})_{\theta\in\Theta}\bigr)
 \ \rightsquigarrow\ 
 \bigl(G,(L_\theta(G))_{\theta\in\Theta}\bigr),
 \qquad G\sim Q_0;
\]
(ii) every likelihood-ratio sequence is uniformly integrable, in the explicit sense that
\[
 \lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_C
 \mathbb E_{P_{C,0}}\!\left[L_{C,\theta}
 \mathbf 1\{L_{C,\theta}>R\}\right]=0
 \quad\text{for every }\theta\in\Theta;
\]
and (iii) nonnegative losses \(\ell_C(\theta,a)\) and \(\ell(\theta,a)\), indexed by \(\Theta\times\mathcal D\), satisfy
\[
 \max_{\theta\in\Theta,\ a\in\mathcal D}
 |\ell_C(\theta,a)-\ell(\theta,a)|\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sup_{C,\theta,a}\ell_C(\theta,a)<\infty.
\]
For a measurable randomized rule \(\delta_C\colon\mathsf X_C\to\Delta_{\mathcal D}\), define
\[
 \mathcal R_{C,\theta}(\delta_C)
 =\mathbb E_{P_{C,\theta}}\!\left[
   \sum_{a\in\mathcal D}\delta_{C,a}\ell_C(\theta,a)
 \right],
 \qquad

Put \(b_C=\mathcal B_C(\delta_C)\).  Assumption (iii) gives a constant \(B<\infty\) such that \(0\leq\ell_C(\theta,a)\leq B\) for every \(C,\theta,a\); increasing \(B\) if necessary also gives \(0\leq\ell(\theta,a)\leq B\).  Hence \(0\leq b_C\leq B\).  Choose a subsequence \((C_j)\) such that
\[
 b_{C_j}\longrightarrow\liminf_{C\to\infty}b_C.
\]

Represent the randomized rule by its action-probability vector
\[
 V_C=(\delta_{C,a})_{a\in\mathcal D}\in\Delta_{\mathcal D}.
\]
By assumption (i), the laws under \(P_{C,0}\) of
\(\bigl(T_C,(L_{C,\theta})_{\theta\in\Theta}\bigr)\) are tight.  The simplex \(\Delta_{\mathcal D}\) is compact because \(\mathcal D\) is finite.  Therefore the joint laws of
\[
 \left(T_{C_j},(L_{C_j,\theta})_{\theta\in\Theta},V_{C_j}\right)
\]
are tight.  Passing to a further subsequence, without changing the displayed limit of \(b_{C_j}\), gives
\[
 \left(T_{C_j},(L_{C_j,\theta})_{\theta\in\Theta},V_{C_j}\right)
 \rightsquigarrow
 \left(G,(L_\theta(G))_{\theta\in\Theta},V\right)
 \tag{1}
\]
under the reference laws.  Let \(\Lambda\) denote the limiting joint law in (1).  Its first two marginals are the marginals fixed by assumption (i), and \(V\in\Delta_{\mathcal D}\) holds \(\Lambda\)-almost surely because the simplex is closed.

We next pass each risk to the limit.  Change of measure and the definition of \(V_C\) give, for every \(\theta\in\Theta\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal R_{C,\theta}(\delta_C)
 &=\mathbb E_{P_{C,\theta}}\!\left[
     \sum_{a\in\mathcal D}V_{C,a}\ell_C(\theta,a)
   \right]\\
 &=\mathbb E_{P_{C,0}}\!\left[
     L_{C,\theta}\sum_{a\in\mathcal D}V_{C,a}
     \ell_C(\theta,a)
   \right].
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{2}
\]
For fixed \(R<\infty\), (1), bounded continuity of
\((x,l,v)\mapsto(l_\theta\wedge R)\sum_a v_a\ell(\theta,a)\), and assumption (iii) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\mathbb E_{P_{C_j,0}}\!\left[
   (L_{C_j,\theta}\wedge R)
   \sum_{a\in\mathcal D}V_{C_j,a}\ell_{C_j}(\theta,a)
 \right]\\
 &\hspace{30mm}\longrightarrow
 \mathbb E_{\Lambda}\!\left[
   (L_\theta(G)\wedge R)
   \sum_{a\in\mathcal D}V_a\ell(\theta,a)
 \right].
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{3}
\]
Indeed, replacing \(\ell_{C_j}\) by \(\ell\) changes the left side by at most
\[
 R\max_{\vartheta\in\Theta,\ a\in\mathcal D}
 |\ell_{C_j}(\vartheta,a)-\ell(\vartheta,a)|,
\]
which tends to zero by assumption (iii).  The truncation error on the finite-experiment side is at most
\[
 B\,\mathbb E_{P_{C_j,0}}\!\left[
 L_{C_j,\theta}\mathbf 1\{L_{C_j,\theta}>R\}
\right],
 \tag{4}
\]
uniformly in \(j\), and (4) tends to zero as \(R\to\infty\) by assumption (ii).  On the limit side the analogous error tends to zero because \(L_\theta(G)\) is a \(Q_0\)-likelihood ratio and hence is nonnegative with
\(\mathbb E_{Q_0}[L_\theta(G)]=1\).  Letting first \(j\to\infty\) in (3) and then \(R\to\infty\), equations (2)--(4) yield
\[
 \mathcal R_{C_j,\theta}(\delta_{C_j})
 \longrightarrow
 \mathbb E_{\Lambda}\!\left[
 L_\theta(G)\sum_{a\in\mathcal D}V_a\ell(\theta,a)
 \right].
 \tag{5}
\]

It remains to turn the possibly enlarged limiting randomization \(V\) into a rule in the Gaussian experiment.  Because \(G\) takes values in the standard Borel space \(\mathbb R^d\), choose measurable versions
\[
 \bar\delta_a(g)=\mathbb E_{\Lambda}[V_a\mid G=g],
 \qquad a\in\mathcal D.
\]
Nonnegativity of the coordinates of \(V\) and \(\sum_aV_a=1\) imply
\(\bar\delta(g)\in\Delta_{\mathcal D}\) for \(Q_0\)-almost every \(g\); redefine it at most on a \(Q_0\)-null set to obtain a measurable randomized rule everywhere.  Since \(L_\theta(G)\) is measurable with respect to \(G\), conditional expectation and then the likelihood-ratio identity give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\Lambda}\!\left[
 L_\theta(G)\sum_aV_a\ell(\theta,a)
 \right]
 &=\mathbb E_{Q_0}\!\left[
 L_\theta(G)\sum_a\bar\delta_a(G)\ell(\theta,a)
 \right]\\
 &=\mathbb E_{Q_\theta}\!\left[
 \sum_a\bar\delta_a(G)\ell(\theta,a)
 \right].
 \tag{6}
 \end{aligned}
\]
The absolute integrability needed in (6) follows from the bound \(B\) and
\(\mathbb E_{Q_0}L_\theta(G)=1\).

Because \(\Theta\) is finite, (5)--(6) may be summed against \(\varpi\).  The choice of the subsequence and the definition of the optimal limit Bayes risk then give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \liminf_{C\to\infty}\mathcal B_C(\delta_C)
 &=\lim_{j\to\infty}b_{C_j}\\
 &=\sum_{\theta\in\Theta}\varpi_\theta
   \mathbb E_{Q_\theta}\!\left[
     \sum_{a\in\mathcal D}\bar\delta_a(G)\ell(\theta,a)
   \right]\\
 &\geq \mathcal B_\infty^*(\varpi).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Finally, for every \(C\), a maximum dominates every probability-weighted average:
\[
 \max_{\theta\in\Theta}\mathcal R_{C,\theta}(\delta_C)
 \geq
 \sum_{\theta\in\Theta}\varpi_\theta
 \mathcal R_{C,\theta}(\delta_C)
 =\mathcal B_C(\delta_C).
\]
Taking lower limits and using the Bayes-risk inequality proves the asserted maximal-risk bound.
